subtitle: In the moving camp of empire, a conqueror watches his realm strain and fray

panels.shot: epic mid-shot from tent entrance looking out over a vast Deccan camp at dusk
panels.action: Aurangzeb Alamgir stands at the flap of a great canvas tent in the Deccan, his aging face stern and lined, looking over endless rows of Mughal tents and campfires under a vast darkening sky.

dialogue.text: Aurangzeb Alamgir, last great Mughal, spends his final decades in a moving tent-city over the Deccan, as victory and decay march side by side.

i18n.hi: औरंगज़ेब आलमगीर, आख़िरी बड़ा मुग़ल, उम्र के आख़िरी बरस दक्खन की चलती तंबू-शहर में काटता है, जहाँ फ़तह और सड़न साथ-साथ चलते हैं

panels.shot: wide bird’s-eye of north India fading into Deccan plateau, with army columns winding south
panels.action: A map-like vista shows the rich plains around the Yamuna and Ganga fading into the rocky Deccan plateau, as tiny Mughal columns snake southward, with Aurangzeb’s small figure on an elephant at their head.

dialogue.text: In 1682, the emperor leaves Delhi and Agra behind, carrying the heart of the Mughal state into the hard stone lands of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: १६८२ में बादशाह दिल्ली-आगरा छोड़ देता है, मुग़ल सल्तनत का दिल उठाकर दक्खन की पत्थरी ज़मीनों में ले आता है

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Aurangzeb on elephant before walls of Bijapur
panels.action: Aurangzeb sits erect upon a caparisoned elephant before the massive bastioned walls of Bijapur, siege trenches and Mughal cannon lines stretching across the dry plain under a fierce sun.

dialogue.text: Before him rise the Adil Shahi walls of Bijapur, proud citadel of a Deccan sultanate that once held Mughal armies at bay.

i18n.hi: उसके आगे उभरती हैं बीजापुर की आदिलशाही फ़ौजी दीवारें, दक्खन की उस शानोशौकत वाली राजधानी की, जिसने कभी मुग़ल फ़ौजों को रोक रखा था

panels.shot: mid-shot inside imperial tent, Aurangzeb over campaign maps with Deccan markings
panels.action: Inside a richly ordered but austere imperial tent, Aurangzeb bends over parchment maps marked with Bijapur, Golconda and Maratha hill forts, small counters showing armies and jagirs laid out across the Deccan.

dialogue.text: For Aurangzeb, the Deccan is more than zeal and rivalry. It is revenue, frontier, image of empire—an old dream of bringing all peninsular kings within one imperial discipline.

i18n.hi: औरंगज़ेब के लिए दक्खन सिर्फ़ जोश या दुश्मनी नहीं, यह आय, सरहद, सल्तनत की शान है—पुराना सपना, कि पूरे प्रायद्वीप के बादशाह एक ही ताज़ के नीचे झुकें

panels.shot: high wide shot of storm-laden sky over Bijapur as gates open in distance
panels.action: Dark clouds gather over Bijapur’s domes as distant city gates stand ajar; Mughal standards rise in the foreground, with Aurangzeb’s silhouette watching from a siege platform.

dialogue.text: In 1686, Bijapur yields. A year later, the Qutb Shahi citadel of Golconda falls. The Deccan sultanates are broken, and their rich lands folded into the Mughal revenue system.

i18n.hi: १६८६ में बीजापुर झुकता है। एक साल बाद क़ुतुबशाही गोलकुंडा भी गिरता है। दक्खनी सुल्तनतें टूटती हैं, उनकी समृद्ध ज़मीनें मुग़ल महसूल में शामिल हो जाती हैं

panels.shot: mid-shot of Aurangzeb in audience tent, surrounded by eager mansabdars
panels.action: Aurangzeb sits on a simple camp throne beneath a canopy, while ranks of mansabdars press forward with hopeful faces, each holding petitions and revenue papers seeking new Deccan assignments.

dialogue.text: With conquest, a flood of expectation. Old warriors and new adventurers crowd for mansabs and jagirs, each slice of land pledged to pay a growing army of claimants.

i18n.hi: फ़तह के साथ उम्मीदों की बाढ़ आती है। पुराने सिपहसालार और नए बाज़ीगर मनसब और जागीर के लिए टूट पड़ते हैं, हर टुकड़ा ज़मीन किसी नए दावेदार की तनख़्वाह से बंधा है

panels.shot: close-up on Aurangzeb’s hand hovering over a jagir list, ink-stained and crowded
panels.action: A parchment jagir roll lies crowded with names and figures; Aurangzeb’s veined hand, ringed and steady, pauses with reed pen above a margin already crammed with notes.

dialogue.text: Soon, as later scholars will see, the numbers tighten like a noose. More salaries promised than the land can safely yield, even with fresh Deccan fields measured and taxed.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही, जैसा बाद के अलिम देखेंगे, हिसाब फाँसी के फंदे सा कसता है। ज़मीन जितना उठा सके, उससे ज़्यादा तनख़्वाहें बाँधी जा चुकी हैं, चाहे नए दक्खनी खेत नापकर टैक्स भी लगाए जाएँ

panels.shot: wide shot of rugged Deccan hills with a Maratha fort in distance, Mughal camp in foreground
panels.action: On a craggy Deccan hill, a small Maratha fort stands defiant, its wooden gates shut; below, the sprawling Mughal camp stretches across the plain, Aurangzeb’s tent at its center like a pale heart.

dialogue.text: Yet with sultanates gone, another power bleeds him. From hill forts and forest tracks, the Marathas under Sambhaji, then Rajaram and Tarabai, harry and fade, taxing the land from under imperial feet.

i18n.hi: पर सुल्तनतें मिटते ही दूसरी ताक़त उसका ख़ून चूसती है। पहाड़ी क़िलों और जंगल-पगडंडियों से, पहले संभाजी, फिर राजाराम और ताराबाई के मराठे चढ़ाई करके ओझल हो जाते हैं, बादशाह के पाँव तले से लगान खींच लेते हैं

panels.shot: dynamic wide of flaming countryside, Mughal column marching while distant riders vanish
panels.action: A Mughal column marches through smoke-hazed countryside, fields scorched and villages emptied; in the distance, tiny Maratha riders disappear over a ridge, leaving only dust behind.

dialogue.text: Aurangzeb’s generals win cities and forts. They also find barren fields, emptied villages, and Maratha bands that strike at caravans and treasuries, then melt, undoing in months what took years to impose.

i18n.hi: औरंगज़ेब के सरदार शहर और क़िले लेते हैं, पर पाते हैं सूखे खेत, खाली गाँव, और मराठा टोलियाँ जो काफ़िलों और ख़ज़ाना-गाड़ियों पर वार कर, ग़ायब हो जाती हैं, महीनों में उस हुक्म को उलट देती हैं जो सालों में क़ायम हुआ

panels.shot: mid-shot of Aurangzeb in prayer mat within tent as rain lashes canvas
panels.action: Rain beats against the canvas walls of a modest imperial tent; inside, Aurangzeb kneels on a plain prayer mat, armor set aside, his lips moving in quiet recitation, lamp light flickering over his worn features.

dialogue.text: Through it all, the emperor lives in canvas and dust. He prays, he fasts, he commands, his own life grown as severe as the campaign itself.

i18n.hi: सारा वक़्त बादशाह तंबुओं और गर्द में रहता है। नमाज़, रोज़ा, फ़रमान—उसकी ज़िंदगी खुद मुहिम जितनी सख़्त हो चुकी है

panels.shot: mid-shot of Aurangzeb dictating a letter, scribe seated before him
panels.action: Aurangzeb sits cross-legged, speaking slowly to a court scribe who writes on folded paper, a small stack of sealed letters beside him, the tent opening showing a gray Deccan dawn.

dialogue.text: From this mobile court flow letters north and east—orders on taxation, remonstrances to sons, reflections that later copyists and translators will preserve and dispute.

i18n.hi: इसी सफ़र करती दरबारगाह से ख़त उत्तर और पूरब उड़ते हैं—माल के हुक्म, बेटों को डाँट-डपट, वो तजुर्बे जिन्हें नकलनवीस और मतरجم आने वाली सदियों में लिखेंगे और बहस करेंगे

panels.shot: close-up on Aurangzeb’s thoughtful face lit by lamplight, letter in background
panels.action: In lamplight, Aurangzeb’s face is caught in a rare moment of stillness, eyes shadowed; behind him on a low desk lies an opened letter bearing his seal, its script neat and dense.

dialogue.text: Later ages will argue which words were truly his at the end, and which belong to pious imagination. The Deccan, however, leaves no doubt on paper: his presence, his orders, his burdens.

i18n.hi: आगे की नस्लें बहस करेंगी कि आख़िर में कौन से अल्फ़ाज़ सच उसके थे, और कौन नेक ख़यालों की पैदाइश। पर दक्खन काग़ज़ पर साफ़ है: उसकी मौजूदगी, उसके हुक्म, उसके बोझ

panels.shot: wide shot of a strained Mughal encampment, with unpaid soldiers murmuring
panels.action: Within the vast camp, clusters of Mughal soldiers stand with folded arms and tense faces near their tents, while officers argue over account scrolls, the distant imperial pavilion looming like a silent judge.

dialogue.text: As the years grind on, arrears deepen. Troops wait for wages that crawl through hostile countryside. Jagirdars squeeze harder, or abandon posts to seek more paying assignments.

i18n.hi: सालों के पीसने से बाक़ियाँ बढ़ती जाती हैं। फ़ौजें तनख़्वाह की राह देखती हैं जो दुश्मन देस से रेंगती हुई पहुँचती है। जागीरदार या तो ज़्यादा निचोड़ते हैं, या ठिकाने छोड़कर ज़्यादा फ़ायदे की ड्यूटी ढूँढने निकल पड़ते हैं

panels.shot: mid-shot of Aurangzeb chastising an official, with revenue reports in hand
panels.action: Aurangzeb stands, eyes sharp with cold anger, holding a revenue report while a bowed official before him clutches his turban in both hands in anxious humility.

dialogue.speaker: aurangzeb_alamgir
dialogue.text: You burden the raiyat, then complain of revolt. Justice is a sharper sword than yours.

i18n.hi: तू रइयत को कुचलता है, फिर बगावत का शिकवा करता है। इंसाफ़ तुम्हारी तलवार से तीखा है

panels.shot: wide shot of massive imperial camp moving across the Deccan plain
panels.action: A long panoramic view shows the Mughal camp on the move: endless lines of tents being struck, camels laden, elephants hauling artillery, with Aurangzeb’s plain palanquin at the core.

dialogue.text: His court never settles. From Ahmadnagar to Brahmapuri, from Parli to Aurangabad, the tent-city crawls, chasing forts, chasing bands, chasing the imperial map he carries in his mind.

i18n.hi: उसका दरबार कभी जड़ नहीं पकड़ता। अहमदनगर से ब्रह्मपुरी, परली से औरंगाबाद तक तंबू-शहर रेंगता है—क़िले पीछा करते हुए, टोलियाँ पीछा करते हुए, उस नक़्शे के पीछे जो वो दिमाग़ में ढोता है

panels.shot: close-up on Aurangzeb’s trembling hands holding prayer beads inside tent
panels.action: Inside the familiar tent, Aurangzeb’s hands, now thin and slightly trembling, move slowly over a string of prayer beads, the canvas above stained by years of rain and smoke.

dialogue.text: By the early 1700s, age and illness press upon him. He has outlived his brothers, many of his sons, and the north he once ruled from marble palaces.

i18n.hi: १७०० के शुरुआती बरसों तक उम्र और बीमारी दोनों उसे दबोच लेते हैं। वो अपने भाइयों से, कई बेटों से, और उस उत्तर से भी लंबा जीता है जिसे कभी संगमरमर के महलों से चलाता था

panels.shot: mid-shot of Aurangzeb in his last days on a simple cot in Ahmadnagar camp
panels.action: Aurangzeb lies on a simple low cot within his Ahmadnagar camp tent, a rolled Qur’an near his pillow; a few attendants stand quietly in the shadows, the tent flap tied against the bright outside light.

dialogue.text: On 3 March 1707, near Ahmadnagar, the long Deccan camp comes to stillness. The emperor who bore his empire on campaign breathes his last, far from Delhi’s red sandstone walls.

i18n.hi: ३ मार्च १७०७ को, अहमदनगर के करीब, लंबा दक्खनी डेरा थम जाता है। जिसने अपनी सल्तनत को हमेशा सफ़र पर ढोया, वो बादशाह दिल्ली की लाल दीवारों से दूर आख़िरी साँस लेता है

panels.shot: wide shot of Aurangzeb’s modest tomb at Khuldabad amidst hills
panels.action: A tranquil scene shows Aurangzeb’s modest open-air grave at Khuldabad, enclosed by a low stone railing, simple and unadorned, set against rolling Deccan hills and a clear sky.

dialogue.text: His body rests in Khuldabad, beneath an open sky, in a grave said to be paid for by the sale of his own woven caps and Qur’ans—the humility he chose, in contrast to the vastness he commanded.

i18n.hi: उसका जिस्म खुलदाबाद में खुले आसमान तले है, उस क़ब्र में, जिसके बारे में कहा जाता है कि उसकी बुनी हुई टोपियों और क़ुरआनों की कमाई से बनी—वो सादगी जो उसने चुनी, उस शान के उलट जिसे कभी हुक्म दिया

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over a fading map of the Mughal empire, cracks spreading from the Deccan
panels.action: A parchment map of the Mughal empire fills the frame, the Deccan annexations prominent; faint cracks and fissures spread outward from the Deccan region toward the northern provinces.

dialogue.text: The Deccan campaigns leave a double legacy: forts taken, sultanates subdued, but an imperial system strained, its jagirs overpromised, its soldiers restless—a reminder that conquest without lasting balance hollows the triumph it seeks.

i18n.hi: दक्खनी मुहिम दोहरी निशानी छोड़ती है: क़िले फ़तह, सुल्तनतें सर झुकाए, पर सल्तनती ढाँचा थककर चरमराया, जागीरें हद से ज़्यादा वादों में फँसी, सिपाही बेक़रार—याद दिलाते हुए कि बेइंतिहा फ़तह, अगर टिकाऊ तवाज़ुन न दे, तो खुद अपनी जीत को खोखला कर देती है

title_i18n.en: Aurangzeb's Last Tent in the Deccan
title_i18n.hi: दक्खन में औरंगज़ेब का आख़िरी ख़ेमा़

subtitle_i18n.en: In the moving camp of empire, a conqueror watches his realm strain and fray
subtitle_i18n.hi: चलती फिरती फ़ौज के बीच, फ़तह का बादशाह देखता है, उसकी सल्तनत दरक रही है
